claim: At embryonic day (E)50, TFAP2C+SOX17+PDPN+ cjPGCs were predominantly localized within the ventral portion of the hindgut endoderm.
source: At this stage, TFAP2C+SOX17+PDPN+ cjPGCs were predominantly localized within the ventral portion of the hindgut endoderm and exhibited round nuclei with generally lower DAPI intensity (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1B and C showing localization of TFAP2C+SOX17+PDPN+ cells in the hindgut endoderm, and by direct statement in the text.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 exhibited round nuclei with generally lower DAPI intensity compared to surrounding cells.
source: At this stage, TFAP2C+SOX17+PDPN+ cjPGCs were predominantly localized within the ventral portion of the hindgut endoderm and exhibited round nuclei with generally lower DAPI intensity (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1C showing arrows denoting nuclei of cjPGCs with lower DAPI intensity than surrounding endodermal cells.

claim: A few scattered cjPGCs were seen in the adjacent hindgut mesenchyme outside of the basement membranes at E50.
source: A few scattered cjPGCs were also seen in the adjacent hindgut mesenchyme outside of the basement membranes, suggestive of the initiation of active migration (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1B showing cjPGCs outside the basement membrane and by direct statement in the text.

claim: The presence of cjPGCs outside the basement membranes is suggestive of the initiation of active migration.
source: A few scattered cjPGCs were also seen in the adjacent hindgut mesenchyme outside of the basement membranes, suggestive of the initiation of active migration (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed data regarding cjPGC localization outside basement membranes.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 were mostly non-proliferative (MKI67-).
source: Additional IF analyses revealed that cjPGCs were mostly non-proliferative (i.e., MKI67-) and co-expressed pluripotency-associated markers (e.g., POU5F1, NANOG), but were negative for SOX2 (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1D showing MKI67 staining and pie chart indicating low MKI67+ cell numbers.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 co-expressed pluripotency-associated markers POU5F1 and NANOG.
source: Additional IF analyses revealed that cjPGCs were mostly non-proliferative (i.e., MKI67-) and co-expressed pluripotency-associated markers (e.g., POU5F1, NANOG), but were negative for SOX2 (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1E showing POU5F1 and NANOG expression in PDPN+ cjPGCs.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 were negative for SOX2.
source: Additional IF analyses revealed that cjPGCs were mostly non-proliferative (i.e., MKI67-) and co-expressed pluripotency-associated markers (e.g., POU5F1, NANOG), but were negative for SOX2 (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B showing absence of SOX2 in TFAP2C+ cjPGCs.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 did not express later germ cell markers DDX4 and DAZL.
source: Notably, cjPGCs did not express later germ cell markers (e.g., DDX4 and DAZL), that are typically observed in testicular germ cells (i.e., prospermatogonia) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1E showing absence of DDX4 and DAZL in PDPN+ cjPGCs at E50.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 showed increased global levels of histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3).
source: IF analysis on cjPGCs showed increased global levels of histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) and reduced global levels of histone H3 lysine 9 dimethylation (H3K9me2), consistent with the germline epigenetic reprogramming that occurs in mice, cynomolgus monkeys, and humans (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Seki et al., 2007; Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1F showing relative fluorescence intensity of H3K27me3 in PDPN+ cjPGCs compared to surrounding somatic cells, and by citation to prior studies.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 showed reduced global levels of histone H3 lysine 9 dimethylation (H3K9me2).
source: IF analysis on cjPGCs showed increased global levels of histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) and reduced global levels of histone H3 lysine 9 dimethylation (H3K9me2), consistent with the germline epigenetic reprogramming that occurs in mice, cynomolgus monkeys, and humans (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Seki et al., 2007; Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1F showing relative fluorescence intensity of H3K9me2 in PDPN+ cjPGCs compared to surrounding somatic cells, and by citation to prior studies.

claim: The epigenetic reprogramming observed in cjPGCs is consistent with germline epigenetic reprogramming that occurs in mice, cynomolgus monkeys, and humans.
source: IF analysis on cjPGCs showed increased global levels of histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) and reduced global levels of histone H3 lysine 9 dimethylation (H3K9me2), consistent with the germline epigenetic reprogramming that occurs in mice, cynomolgus monkeys, and humans (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Seki et al., 2007; Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies in mice, cynomolgus monkeys, and humans (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Seki et al., 2007).

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing captured 34,458 cells from two marmoset embryos at E50.
source: In total, 34,458 cells (6 libraries comprising 12,665 and 21,793 cells from embryos A and B, respectively) were captured for downstream analyses (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–I).
evidence: Supported by the description of sequencing results in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A cluster representing cjPGCs was identified and marked by TFAP2C, SOX17, and PDPN expression.
source: Using known markers and differentially expressed genes (DEGs), we identified a cluster representing cjPGCs (cluster 11 marked by TFAP2C, SOX17, and PDPN) along with other clusters including CLDN5+ endothelium (cluster 3), OSR1+PAX8+ intermediate mesoderm (cluster 4), FOXF1+ lateral plate mesoderm (cluster 5), and SOX2+ neutral tube (cluster 9) (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by UMAP plot in Figure 2A showing cluster 11 as cjPGCs and violin plots in Figure 2C showing expression of TFAP2C, SOX17, and PDPN.

claim: cjPGCs expressed potential germ cell specifier/regulator genes including DND1, KIT, PRDM1, SOX15, SOX17, and TFAP2C.
source: Analysis of DEGs in the cjPGC cluster revealed upregulated expression of potential germ cell specifier/regulator genes (e.g., DND1, KIT, PRDM1, SOX15, SOX17, TFAP2C), pluripotency-associated genes (e.g., DPPA3, KLF4, NANOG, POU5F1, TFCP2L1, UTF1, ZFP42), mesoderm/endoderm-associated genes (e.g., GATA4, TBXT), and other germ cell-related markers (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 2B and boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression of these genes in cjPGCs.

claim: cjPGCs expressed pluripotency-associated genes including DPPA3, KLF4, NANOG, POU5F1, TFCP2L1, UTF1, and ZFP42.
source: Analysis of DEGs in the cjPGC cluster revealed upregulated expression of potential germ cell specifier/regulator genes (e.g., DND1, KIT, PRDM1, SOX15, SOX17, TFAP2C), pluripotency-associated genes (e.g., DPPA3, KLF4, NANOG, POU5F1, TFCP2L1, UTF1, ZFP42), mesoderm/endoderm-associated genes (e.g., GATA4, TBXT), and other germ cell-related markers (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 2B and boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression of these genes in cjPGCs.

claim: cjPGCs expressed mesoderm/endoderm-associated genes including GATA4 and TBXT.
source: Analysis of DEGs in the cjPGC cluster revealed upregulated expression of potential germ cell specifier/regulator genes (e.g., DND1, KIT, PRDM1, SOX15, SOX17, TFAP2C), pluripotency-associated genes (e.g., DPPA3, KLF4, NANOG, POU5F1, TFCP2L1, UTF1, ZFP42), mesoderm/endoderm-associated genes (e.g., GATA4, TBXT), and other germ cell-related markers (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 2B and boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression of these genes in cjPGCs.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in cjPGCs were enriched with GO terms such as 'germ cell development'.
source: Accordingly, these genes were enriched with those bearing GO terms such as 'germ cell development' (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by gene ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: SOX2 was not expressed by cjPGCs at E50.
source: Among pluripotency-associated genes, SOX2 was not expressed by cjPGCs, and PRDM14 was expressed only weakly, a feature conserved with other primates (i.e., humans, cynomolgus monkeys; Figure 2E; Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing no SOX2 expression in cjPGCs and by citations to prior studies in humans and cynomolgus monkeys (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2015).

claim: PRDM14 was expressed only weakly in cjPGCs at E50.
source: Among pluripotency-associated genes, SOX2 was not expressed by cjPGCs, and PRDM14 was expressed only weakly, a feature conserved with other primates (i.e., humans, cynomolgus monkeys; Figure 2E; Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing low PRDM14 expression in cjPGCs and by citations to prior studies in humans and cynomolgus monkeys (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2015).

claim: The lack of SOX2 expression and weak PRDM14 expression in cjPGCs is a feature conserved with other primates including humans and cynomolgus monkeys.
source: Among pluripotency-associated genes, SOX2 was not expressed by cjPGCs, and PRDM14 was expressed only weakly, a feature conserved with other primates (i.e., humans, cynomolgus monkeys; Figure 2E; Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies in humans and cynomolgus monkeys (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2015).

claim: Expression of key proliferation markers was low in cjPGCs at E50.
source: Expression of key proliferation markers was low, in agreement with MKI67 labeling (Figure 1D), suggesting that cjPGCs are largely quiescent (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Supported by violin plots in Figure 1—figure supplement 1J showing low expression of proliferation markers and by MKI67 labeling data in Figure 1D.

claim: cjPGCs at E50 are largely quiescent.
source: Expression of key proliferation markers was low, in agreement with MKI67 labeling (Figure 1D), suggesting that cjPGCs are largely quiescent (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is an inference based on low expression of proliferation markers and MKI67 labeling.

claim: Germ cell markers known to be activated upon arrival at the gonads (DAZL, DDX4, RNF17) were not expressed in cjPGCs at E50.
source: Germ cell markers known to be activated upon arrival at the gonads were not expressed (e.g., DAZL, DDX4, RNF17) (Figure 2E), consistent with the pre-migratory state of these cells (Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing no expression of DAZL, DDX4, and RNF17 in cjPGCs, and by citations to prior studies (Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017).

claim: The lack of expression of DAZL, DDX4, and RNF17 in cjPGCs at E50 is consistent with the pre-migratory state of these cells.
source: Germ cell markers known to be activated upon arrival at the gonads were not expressed (e.g., DAZL, DDX4, RNF17) (Figure 2E), consistent with the pre-migratory state of these cells (Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of gonadal stage markers and supported by citations to prior studies (Sasaki et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017).

claim: cjPGCs expressed low levels of enzymes for the deposition of H3K9me2 (EHMT2, SUV39H1, SUV39H2).
source: In agreement with globally low H3K9me2 levels (Figure 1F), cjPGCs expressed low levels of enzymes for the deposition of H3K9me2 (e.g., EHMT2, SUV39H1, SUV39H2), and instead, expressed several H3K9 demethylases (e.g., KDM1A/3A/3B/4A) (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression levels of these enzymes in cjPGCs.

claim: cjPGCs expressed several H3K9 demethylases including KDM1A, KDM3A, KDM3B, and KDM4A.
source: In agreement with globally low H3K9me2 levels (Figure 1F), cjPGCs expressed low levels of enzymes for the deposition of H3K9me2 (e.g., EHMT2, SUV39H1, SUV39H2), and instead, expressed several H3K9 demethylases (e.g., KDM1A/3A/3B/4A) (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression levels of these demethylases in cjPGCs.

claim: cjPGCs expressed EED, EZH2, and SUZ12, enzymes involved in the deposition of H3K27me3.
source: Among enzymes involved in the deposition of H3K27me3, cjPGCs expressed EED, EZH2, SUZ12, whereas EZH1 expression was low (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression levels of these enzymes in cjPGCs.

claim: EZH1 expression was low in cjPGCs at E50.
source: Among enzymes involved in the deposition of H3K27me3, cjPGCs expressed EED, EZH2, SUZ12, whereas EZH1 expression was low (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing low EZH1 expression in cjPGCs.

claim: The expression pattern of H3K27me3-related enzymes in cjPGCs is consistent with PGCLCs/PGCs in humans and cynomolgus monkeys.
source: These findings are consistent with PGCLCs/PGCs in humans and cynomolgus monkeys (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies in humans and cynomolgus monkeys (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015).

claim: TET1 was expressed at high levels in cjPGCs at E50.
source: Among genes related to DNA demethylation, TET1 was expressed at high levels, whereas TET2 and TET3 were expressed at low levels (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing high TET1 expression in cjPGCs.

claim: TET2 and TET3 were expressed at low levels in cjPGCs at E50.
source: Among genes related to DNA demethylation, TET1 was expressed at high levels, whereas TET2 and TET3 were expressed at low levels (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing low TET2 and TET3 expression in cjPGCs.

claim: DNMT1 and DNMT3A were expressed at modest levels in cjPGCs at E50.
source: DNMT1 and DNMT3A were expressed at modest levels, whereas UHRF1, DNMT3L, DNMT3B were markedly lower, suggesting that passive demethylation might be operative due to diminished UHRF1 activity required for maintenance DNA methylation, as suggested in other species (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Kagiwada et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2015; Gkountela et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing expression levels of DNMT1 and DNMT3A in cjPGCs.

claim: UHRF1, DNMT3L, and DNMT3B were expressed at markedly lower levels in cjPGCs at E50.
source: DNMT1 and DNMT3A were expressed at modest levels, whereas UHRF1, DNMT3L, DNMT3B were markedly lower, suggesting that passive demethylation might be operative due to diminished UHRF1 activity required for maintenance DNA methylation, as suggested in other species (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Kagiwada et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2015; Gkountela et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 2E showing low expression levels of UHRF1, DNMT3L, and DNMT3B in cjPGCs.

claim: Passive demethylation might be operative in cjPGCs due to diminished UHRF1 activity required for maintenance DNA methylation.
source: DNMT1 and DNMT3A were expressed at modest levels, whereas UHRF1, DNMT3L, DNMT3B were markedly lower, suggesting that passive demethylation might be operative due to diminished UHRF1 activity required for maintenance DNA methylation, as suggested in other species (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Kagiwada et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2015; Gkountela et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on low UHRF1 expression and supported by citations to prior studies in other species (Sasaki et al., 2016; Tang et al., 2015; Kagiwada et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2015; Gkountela et al., 2015).

claim: Three cjiPSC cell lines (20201_6, 20201_7, and 20201_10) were established by reprogramming of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs).
source: Three cell lines, 20201_6, 20201_7, and 20201_10, were established by reprogramming of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) (Materials and methods).
evidence: Directly stated in the text.

claim: Whole-exome sequencing confirmed that the established cjiPSCs originated from the intended PBMC donor (ID number, 38189).
source: Although hematological chimerism is frequently observed in marmosets (Ross et al., 2007; Benirschke et al., 1962), whole-exome sequencing confirmed that the established cjiPSCs originated from the intended PBMC donor (ID number, 38189) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Supported by unsupervised hierarchical clustering and allele frequency distribution data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B, and by citations to prior studies on marmoset chimerism (Ross et al., 2007; Benirschke et al., 1962).

claim: Hematological chimerism is frequently observed in marmosets.
source: Although hematological chimerism is frequently observed in marmosets (Ross et al., 2007; Benirschke et al., 1962), whole-exome sequencing confirmed that the established cjiPSCs originated from the intended PBMC donor (ID number, 38189) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies (Ross et al., 2007; Benirschke et al., 1962).

claim: FF cjiPSCs could be stably maintained over multiple passages (more than 20 passages) when passaged every 4–6 days in the presence of Y27632.
source: Under these conditions, FF cjiPSCs could be stably maintained over multiple passages (more than 20 passages) when passaged every 4–6 days in the presence of Y27632, a ROCK inhibitor.
evidence: Directly stated in the text.

claim: FF cjiPSCs bore a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, were tightly packed in colonies with sharp borders and exhibited flat morphology.
source: FF cjiPSCs bore a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, were tightly packed in colonies with sharp borders and exhibited flat morphology, each of which are characteristic features of primate primed-state pluripotent cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by bright field images in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing colony morphology.

claim: The morphological features of FF cjiPSCs are characteristic of primate primed-state pluripotent cells.
source: FF cjiPSCs bore a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, were tightly packed in colonies with sharp borders and exhibited flat morphology, each of which are characteristic features of primate primed-state pluripotent cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of primate primed-state pluripotent cell characteristics.

claim: cjiPSCs were mycoplasma-free.
source: These cells were mycoplasma-free, exhibited normal 46, XY karyotypes, and uniformly expressed key pluripotency-associated genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: Supported by diagnostic PCR results in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D showing absence of mycoplasma genomic DNA.

claim: cjiPSCs exhibited normal 46, XY karyotypes.
source: These cells were mycoplasma-free, exhibited normal 46, XY karyotypes, and uniformly expressed key pluripotency-associated genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: Supported by G-band karyotype analysis results in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E showing normal 46, XY karyotypes.

claim: cjiPSCs uniformly expressed key pluripotency-associated genes.
source: These cells were mycoplasma-free, exhibited normal 46, XY karyotypes, and uniformly expressed key pluripotency-associated genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F showing expression of NANOG, POU5F1, and SOX2, and by qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: OF cjiPSCs tended to differentiate at the center or periphery of colonies 4–5 days after passaging.
source: Notably, similar to FF culture, conventional OF cultures allowed long-term propagation of cjiPSCs. However, OF cjiPSCs tended to differentiate at the center or periphery of colonies 4–5 days after passaging (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: Supported by bright field images and AP staining in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B showing areas of differentiation.

claim: OF cjiPSCs required clump passaging because single-cell passaging decreased colony formation after two passages.
source: Moreover, OF cjiPSCs required clump passaging because single-cell passaging decreased colony formation after two passages (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by colony formation efficiency data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: OF cjiPSCs exhibited modest upregulation of mesodermal genes (T, EOMES, MIXL1) and endodermal genes (FOXA2, SOX17) compared to FF cjiPSCs.
source: Accordingly, OF cjiPSCs exhibited modest upregulation of mesodermal (e.g., T, EOMES, MIXL1) and endodermal genes (e.g., FOXA2, SOX17) compared to those maintained under FF conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D showing gene expression levels.

claim: Inhibition of WNT signaling stabilizes primate iPSC/ESC cultures.
source: Previous studies showed that inhibition of WNT signaling stabilizes primate iPSC/ESC cultures (Sakai et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies (Sakai et al., 2020; Kim et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2015).

claim: OF cjiPSCs cultured with PluriSTEM containing IWR1 (OF/IWR1) maintained an undifferentiated morphology and pluripotency-associated gene expression.
source: Notably, OF cjiPSCs cultured with PluriSTEM containing IWR1 (OF/IWR1) maintained an undifferentiated morphology and pluripotency-associated gene expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E, F, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Under OF/IWR1 culture conditions, mesoderm/endoderm genes were suppressed compared with conventional OF culture.
source: Under this condition, mesoderm/endoderm genes were suppressed compared with conventional OF culture.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of gene expression data between OF and OF/IWR1 conditions.

claim: OF/IWR1 culture conditions allowed efficient single-cell passaging.
source: Moreover, OF/IWR1 culture conditions allowed efficient single-cell passaging (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by colony formation efficiency data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Addition of IWR1 to OF culture conditions suppressed spontaneous differentiation, but the effects were not as great as when PluriSTEM was used as a basal medium.
source: While we also found that addition of IWR1 to OF culture conditions previously utilized to grow cynomolgus monkey ESCs (AITS+IF20: advancedRPMI1640 and Neurobasal [1:1] supplemented with AllbuMax [1.6%], 1× ITS [Insulin, Transferrin, Selenium], IWR1 [2.5 μM], and bFGF [20 ng/ml]) suppressed spontaneous differentiation, the effects were not as great as when PluriSTEM was used as a basal medium (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, F).
evidence: Supported by AP staining images in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Two independent Wnt antagonists, IWR and XAV939, increased expression of pluripotency-associated surface markers SSEA3 and SSEA4 in cjiPSCs.
source: Consistent with the role of Wnt inhibition in suppressing spontaneous cjiPSCs differentiation, two independent Wnt antagonists, IWR and XAV939, increased expression of pluripotency-associated surface markers, SSEA3 and SSEA4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G, H).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometric analyses in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G and H showing increased SSEA3 and SSEA4 expression.

claim: A trilineage differentiation assay confirmed the potential of cjiPSCs to differentiate into all three germ layers.
source: Although cjiPSCs cultured under various conditions differed in the expression of some genes, all cjiPSCs expressed key pluripotency-associated markers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F, Figure 3—figure supplement 2D–H), and a trilineage differentiation assay confirmed their potential to differentiate into all three germ layers (Figure 3—figure supplement 2I, J).
evidence: Supported by bright field images of embryoid bodies in Figure 3—figure supplement 2I and qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2J showing expression of markers for all three germ layers.

claim: FF cjiPSCs treated with a PGCLC induction cocktail formed aggregates with a markedly cystic appearance and did not generate SOX17+TFAP2C+ cjPGCLCs.
source: For this, we first treated FF cjiPSCs with a PGCLC induction cocktail (i.e., BMP4, LIF, stem cell factor [SCF], epidermal growth factor [EGF], Y27632) in GK15 (Glasgow minimal essential medium [GMEM] supplemented with 15% KSR) or aRB27 (advanced RPMI1640 and supplemented with 1% B27) basal medium. Under these conditions, cjiPSCs formed aggregates with a markedly cystic appearance and did not generate SOX17+TFAP2C+ cjPGCLCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B), suggesting that they may not have germline competency.
evidence: Supported by bright field images and immunofluorescence images in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B showing cystic aggregates and absence of SOX17+TFAP2C+ cells.

claim: FF cjiPSCs may not have germline competency.
source: Under these conditions, cjiPSCs formed aggregates with a markedly cystic appearance and did not generate SOX17+TFAP2C+ cjPGCLCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B), suggesting that they may not have germline competency.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the failure to generate cjPGCLCs from FF cjiPSCs.

claim: Upon floating culture with a PGCLC induction cocktail, ~3–4% PDPN+ITGA6weak+ cells emerged from OF cjiPSCs starting at d4 of induction.
source: Remarkably, upon floating culture with a PGCLC induction cocktail in GK15 or aRB27, ~3–4% PDPN+ITGA6weak+ cells emerged as a distinct population starting at d4 of induction, although the frequency of such cells generally declined after d4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by FACS analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and boxplot in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D showing percentages of PDPN+ITGA6+ cells.

claim: The frequency of PDPN+ITGA6weak+ cells from OF cjiPSCs generally declined after d4 of induction.
source: Remarkably, upon floating culture with a PGCLC induction cocktail in GK15 or aRB27, ~3–4% PDPN+ITGA6weak+ cells emerged as a distinct population starting at d4 of induction, although the frequency of such cells generally declined after d4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D showing decline in percentages of PDPN+ITGA6+ cells after d4.

claim: Sectioning of aggregates from OF cjiPSCs at d4 revealed small clusters of PDPN+ cells uniformly expressing cjPGC markers (TFAP2C, SOX17, PRDM1, NANOG, and POU5F1).
source: Sectioning of these aggregates at d4 revealed small clusters of PDPN+ cells uniformly expressing cjPGC markers (TFAP2C, SOX17, PRDM1, NANOG, and POU5F1), which was further confirmed by quantitative PCR (qPCR) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, E, F).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3F.

claim: Upon induction in floating culture, OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs readily formed tighter and more uniform size/shape aggregates compared to those induced from OF cjiPSCs.
source: Upon induction in floating culture, cjiPSCs readily formed tighter and more uniform size/shape aggregates compared to those induced from OF cjiPSCs (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by bright field images in Figure 3B showing aggregate morphology.

claim: The induction efficiency of cjPGCLCs from OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs was significantly improved, with ~15–40% cells becoming PDPN+ITGA6weak+ at d4 and d6 of induction.
source: Moreover, under this condition, the induction efficiency of cjPGCLCs was significantly improved, with ~15–40% cells becoming PDPN+ITGA6weak+ at d4 and d6 of induction (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3G, H).
evidence: Supported by FACS plots in Figure 3B, boxplot in Figure 3C, and FACS analyses in Figure 3—figure supplement 3G and H showing percentages of PDPN+ITGA6weak+ cells.

claim: The median yield of PDPN+ cells per aggregate from OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs was ~600 at d4 and d6, but declined thereafter.
source: Although variable across experiments, the median yield of PDPN+ cells per aggregate was ~600 at d4 and d6, but declined thereafter (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 3C showing number of PDPN+ cells per aggregate.

claim: IF of sections of aggregates from OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs at d4 revealed multifocal large clusters of PDPN+ cells uniformly expressing key early germ cell markers (SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, POU5F1, NANOG).
source: IF of sections of aggregates at d4 revealed multifocal large clusters of PDPN+ cells uniformly expressing key early germ cell markers (e.g., SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, POU5F1, NANOG) (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 3D showing expression of these markers in PDPN+ cells.

claim: PDPN can serve as a highly specific surface marker of cjPGCLCs that will allow for isolation of cjPGCLCs for downstream analyses.
source: Notably, this finding suggests that PDPN can serve as a highly specific surface marker of cjPGCLCs that will allow for isolation of cjPGCLCs for downstream analyses.
evidence: This is an inference based on the uniform expression of PDPN in cells expressing cjPGC markers.

claim: Isolated PDPN+ cjPGCLCs expressed pluripotency-associated genes (POU5F1, NANOG) and PGC specifier/early marker genes (SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, NANOS3).
source: In support, qPCR of isolated PDPN+ cjPGCLCs also expressed pluripotency-associated genes (i.e., POU5F1, NANOG), PGC specifier/early marker genes (i.e., SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, and NANOS3) and lacked detectable SOX2 and late germ cell marker (i.e., DDX4, DAZL) (Figure 3E), features similar to pre-migratory PGCs (Figures 1D and 2E; Sasaki et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data in Figure 3E showing gene expression levels.

claim: Isolated PDPN+ cjPGCLCs lacked detectable SOX2 and late germ cell markers (DDX4, DAZL).
source: In support, qPCR of isolated PDPN+ cjPGCLCs also expressed pluripotency-associated genes (i.e., POU5F1, NANOG), PGC specifier/early marker genes (i.e., SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, and NANOS3) and lacked detectable SOX2 and late germ cell marker (i.e., DDX4, DAZL) (Figure 3E), features similar to pre-migratory PGCs (Figures 1D and 2E; Sasaki et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data in Figure 3E showing no detectable expression of SOX2, DDX4, and DAZL.

claim: The gene expression features of isolated PDPN+ cjPGCLCs are similar to pre-migratory PGCs.
source: In support, qPCR of isolated PDPN+ cjPGCLCs also expressed pluripotency-associated genes (i.e., POU5F1, NANOG), PGC specifier/early marker genes (i.e., SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, and NANOS3) and lacked detectable SOX2 and late germ cell marker (i.e., DDX4, DAZL) (Figure 3E), features similar to pre-migratory PGCs (Figures 1D and 2E; Sasaki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of gene expression patterns between cjPGCLCs and pre-migratory PGCs, supported by citation to prior study (Sasaki et al., 2016).

claim: Sorted d6 PDPN+ cjPGCLCs cultured on a STO-feeder layer in DK15 medium containing 2.5% FBS, SCF, FGF2, and forskolin formed loosely arranged clusters.
source: Specifically, we cultured sorted d6 PDPN+ cjPGCLCs on a STO-feeder layer in DK15 medium containing 2.5% fetal bovine serum (FBS), SCF, FGF2, and forskolin. Plated cjPGCLCs formed loosely arranged clusters, which increased in size and became confluent by expansion culture day (c)10 (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by bright field images in Figure 4B showing cluster formation.

claim: Plated cjPGCLCs increased in size and became confluent by expansion culture day (c)10.
source: Plated cjPGCLCs formed loosely arranged clusters, which increased in size and became confluent by expansion culture day (c)10 (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by bright field images in Figure 4B showing progression of cluster growth.

claim: Expansion cultured cjPGCLCs expressed markers of early cjPGC/PGCLCs but did not possess late germ cell markers (DDX4, DAZL).
source: These cells expressed markers of early cjPGC/PGCLCs but did not possess late germ cell markers (i.e., DDX4, DAZL), suggesting that they retain the cellular state of cjPGCLCs (Figure 4C–E, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by FACS analysis in Figure 4C, immunofluorescence images in Figure 4D, and qPCR data in Figure 4E.

claim: Expansion cultured cjPGCLCs retain the cellular state of cjPGCLCs.
source: These cells expressed markers of early cjPGC/PGCLCs but did not possess late germ cell markers (i.e., DDX4, DAZL), suggesting that they retain the cellular state of cjPGCLCs (Figure 4C–E, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern of early and late germ cell markers.

claim: Expansion cultured cjPGCLCs could be passaged approximately every 10 days by dissociation and FACS of PDPN+ cells.
source: Moreover, these cells could be passaged approximately every 10 days by dissociation and fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) of PDPN+ cells and exhibited exponential growth for at least 30 days (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: Supported by FACS analyses in Figure 4F and growth curve in Figure 4G.

claim: Expansion cultured cjPGCLCs exhibited exponential growth for at least 30 days.
source: Moreover, these cells could be passaged approximately every 10 days by dissociation and fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) of PDPN+ cells and exhibited exponential growth for at least 30 days (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: Supported by growth curve in Figure 4G showing exponential increase in cell numbers.

claim: DPPA3 showed modest upregulation during 30 days of expansion culture of cjPGCLCs, similar to hPGCLCs under expansion culture.
source: Although marker expression pattern was largely unchanged during 30 days of expansion culture, DPPA3 showed modest upregulation, similar to hPGCLCs under expansion culture (Figure 4H).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data in Figure 4H showing DPPA3 expression over time, and by comparison to human PGCLCs.

claim: ITGA6 exhibited modest upregulation during expansion culture of cjPGCLCs.
source: ITGA6, which is a surface marker weakly expressed on cjPGCLCs, also exhibited modest upregulation along the time course (Figure 4H).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data in Figure 4H showing ITGA6 expression over time.

claim: After 2 days of floating culture, xenogeneic reconstituted testes (xrTestes) formed tight aggregates.
source: After 2 days of floating culture, xenogeneic reconstituted testes (xrTestes) formed tight aggregates, which were subsequently maintained by air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: Supported by bright field images in Figure 5B showing tight aggregates at day 2.

claim: At day 15 of ALI culture, reconstituted testicular cords surrounded by NR2F2+ interstitial cells were observed in xrTestis cultures.
source: At day 15 of ALI culture, we observed reconstituted testicular cords surrounded by NR2F2+ interstitial cells in xrTestis cultures (Figure 5C, Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 5C showing testicular cord structure and NR2F2+ cells.

claim: At day 15 of ALI culture, there were a number of TFAP2C+POU5F1+NANOG+ cjPGCLCs, which primarily localized peripheral to SOX9+ mouse-derived Sertoli cell nuclei.
source: Notably, there were a number of TFAP2C+POU5F1+NANOG+ cjPGCLCs, which primarily localized peripheral to SOX9+ mouse-derived Sertoli cell nuclei (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 5C showing localization of TFAP2C+POU5F1+NANOG+ cells relative to SOX9+ cells.

claim: xrTestes maintained until day 30 of ALI culture revealed prominent proliferation of TFAP2C+ germ cells, which forced SOX9+ Sertoli cells toward the center of the testicular cords.
source: In addition, xrTestes maintained until day 30 of ALI culture revealed prominent proliferation of TFAP2C+ germ cells, which forced SOX9+ Sertoli cells toward the center of the testicular cords (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 5C showing increased TFAP2C+ cells and repositioning of SOX9+ cells at day 30.

claim: At day 30 of ALI culture, a few scattered DAZL+DDX4+SOX17+POU5F1+TFAP2C+SOX2- cells were found in xrTestes, suggesting progression into early prospermatogonia.
source: Remarkably, we found a few scattered DAZL+DDX4+SOX17+POU5F1+TFAP2C+SOX2- cells (DDX4+TFAP2C+ cells [4/123, 3.3% among all TFAP2C+ cells] and DAZL+TFAP2C+ cells [2/232, 0.86% among all TFAP2C+ cells]), suggesting progression into early prospermatogonia (Figure 5C; Hwang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 5D showing cells expressing these markers, and by citation to prior study (Hwang et al., 2020).

claim: cjPGCLCs can be integrated in the testicular niche and are capable of further expansion and differentiation.
source: Together, these data indicate that cjPGCLCs can be integrated in the testicular niche and are capable of further expansion and differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed proliferation and differentiation of cjPGCLCs in xrTestis culture.

claim: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering classified the cells during cjPGCLCs induction largely into two clusters, one with FF, FF/IWR1, and OF cjiPSCs and the other with cjPGCLCs and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs.
source: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering (UHC) classified the cells during cjPGCLCs induction largely into two clusters, one with FF, FF/IWR1, and OF cjiPSCs and the other with cjPGCLCs and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, which was also supported by Pearson correlation among clusters (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by unsupervised hierarchical clustering dendrogram in Figure 6A and Pearson correlation heatmap in Figure 6B.

claim: There were no significant differences in gene expression between FF and FF/IWR1 cjiPSCs.
source: There were no significant differences in gene expression between FF and FF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, suggesting that IWR1 does not significantly alter the cellular properties of FF cjiPSCs (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by PCA plot in Figure 6C showing overlap of FF and FF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, and scatter plot in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B showing high correlation.

claim: IWR1 does not significantly alter the cellular properties of FF cjiPSCs.
source: There were no significant differences in gene expression between FF and FF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, suggesting that IWR1 does not significantly alter the cellular properties of FF cjiPSCs (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of significant gene expression differences between FF and FF/IWR1 cjiPSCs.

claim: OF and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs were positioned closer to cjPGCLCs in PC space, with OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs being closest to d2 cjPGCLCs.
source: Notably, OF and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs were positioned closer to cjPGCLCs in PC space, with OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs being closest to d2 cjPGCLCs, consistent with their higher competency to differentiate into cjPGCLCs (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by PCA plot in Figure 6C showing relative positioning of samples.

claim: The positioning of OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs closest to d2 cjPGCLCs in PC space is consistent with their higher competency to differentiate into cjPGCLCs.
source: Notably, OF and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs were positioned closer to cjPGCLCs in PC space, with OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs being closest to d2 cjPGCLCs, consistent with their higher competency to differentiate into cjPGCLCs (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between transcriptomic similarity and differentiation competency.

claim: OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs bore gene expression signatures characteristic of primed-state pluripotency, similar to that seen in FF or OF cjiPSCs.
source: OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs bore gene expression signatures characteristic of primed-state pluripotency, similar to that seen in FF or OF cjiPSCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C; Nakamura et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C showing expression of primed-state markers, and by citation to prior study (Nakamura et al., 2016).

claim: There is a modest upregulation of TFAP2C and PRDM14 in OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, which might contribute to their high germline competency.
source: Notably, while most key germ cell genes were not significantly upregulated, there is a modest upregulation of TFAP2C and PRDM14 in OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, which might contribute to their high germline competency (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C showing expression of TFAP2C and PRDM14.

claim: Genes primarily upregulated as FF cjiPSCs transitioned to OF and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs were enriched with GO terms including 'protein destabilization' or 'ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process'.
source: Pairwise comparison of gene expression revealed that genes were primarily upregulated as FF cjiPSCs transitioned to OF and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D). GO terms among the enriched genes in OF and OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs included 'protein destabilization' or 'ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process' (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by scatter plots and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Expression of most genes related to ubiquitin-proteasome system was sustained until d2 cjPGCLCs, suggesting that changes associated with UPS-mediated protein turnover might confer a permissive cellular environment for cjPGCLCs specification.
source: Expression of most of these genes was sustained until d2 cjPGCLCs, suggesting that changes associated with ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS)-mediated protein turnover might confer a permissive cellular environment for cjPGCLCs specification (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: Supported by scatter plots in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and F showing sustained expression of UPS-related genes in d2 cjPGCLCs.

claim: Genes in cluster 1 were enriched with GO terms such as 'inner cell mass cell proliferation' or 'stem cell population maintenance', consistent with their pluripotent nature.
source: Genes in cluster 1 represented those with relatively high expression in cjiPSCs, but which are downregulated during differentiation into cjPGCLCs. Those genes were enriched with GO terms such as 'inner cell mass cell proliferation' or 'stem cell population maintenance', consistent with their pluripotent nature (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by heatmap and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 6D.

claim: Genes in cluster 2 included key germ cell genes (DND1, NANOS3, PRDM1, SOX17, TFAP2C) and GO terms included 'germ cell development'.
source: Genes in cluster 2 were those upregulated along the trajectory and included key germ cell genes (e.g., DND1, NANOS3, PRDM1, SOX17, TFAP2C) and GO terms included 'germ cell development'.
evidence: Supported by heatmap and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 6D.

claim: GO terms for genes in cluster 2 included 'DNA methylation' or 'histone methylation', consistent with the dynamic epigenetic remodeling observed in developing PGCs.
source: Moreover, GO terms such as 'DNA methylation' or 'histone methylation' were also seen, consistent with the dynamic epigenetic remodeling observed in developing PGCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment of epigenetic-related GO terms and established knowledge of PGC development.

claim: Genes in cluster 3 were primary upregulated in 2D expansion culture cjPGCLCs and included an enriched GO term, 'response to oxidative stress', which might suggest changes associated with culture adaptation.
source: Genes in cluster 3 were those primary upregulated in 2D expansion culture cjPGCLCs and included an enriched GO term, 'response to oxidative stress', which might suggest changes associated with culture adaptation.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the enrichment of 'response to oxidative stress' GO term in expansion culture cjPGCLCs.

claim: Genes in cluster 4 were transiently upregulated in d2 cjPGCLCs and included endoderm and mesoderm markers (EOMES, HAND1, MESP1, MIXL1, NODAL, SNAL1).
source: Finally, genes in cluster 4 were those transiently upregulated in d2 cjPGCLCs. These genes included endoderm and mesoderm markers (e.g., EOMES, HAND1, MESP1, MIXL1, NODAL, SNAL1) and were enriched with GO terms such as 'mesoderm formation' and 'cellular response to BMP stimulus', suggesting that cjPGCLC induction may be transiently accompanied by somatic programs, as previously observed following PGCLC induction in other primates (Figure 6D–F; Sasaki et al., 2015; Sakai et al., 2020; Irie et al., 2015; Kobayashi et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by heatmap and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 6D, and expression plots in Figure 6E and F.

claim: cjPGCLC induction may be transiently accompanied by somatic programs, as previously observed following PGCLC induction in other primates.
source: Finally, genes in cluster 4 were those transiently upregulated in d2 cjPGCLCs. These genes included endoderm and mesoderm markers (e.g., EOMES, HAND1, MESP1, MIXL1, NODAL, SNAL1) and were enriched with GO terms such as 'mesoderm formation' and 'cellular response to BMP stimulus', suggesting that cjPGCLC induction may be transiently accompanied by somatic programs, as previously observed following PGCLC induction in other primates (Figure 6D–F; Sasaki et al., 2015; Sakai et al., 2020; Irie et al., 2015; Kobayashi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the transient upregulation of mesodermal genes and supported by citations to prior studies in other primates (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sakai et al., 2020; Irie et al., 2015; Kobayashi et al., 2017).

claim: Key germ cell specifier genes (SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, NANOS3) started to increase in expression and SOX2 was swiftly downregulated in d2 cjPGCLCs.
source: We noted that key germ cell specifier genes (e.g., SOX17, TFAP2C, PRDM1, NANOS3) started to increase in expression and SOX2 was swiftly downregulated in d2 cjPGCLCs (Figure 6G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by expression plots in Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: TBXT, which is only transiently activated in mPGCLCs, continued to be expressed after d2 in cjPGCLCs, similar to hPGCLCs.
source: TBXT, which is only transiently activated in mPGCLCs, continued to be expressed after d2, similar to hPGCLCs (Figure 6G; Sasaki et al., 2015; Sakai et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by expression plot in Figure 6G showing sustained TBXT expression, and by citations to prior studies in mice and humans (Sasaki et al., 2015; Sakai et al., 2020).

claim: DDX4 and DAZL, germ cell markers expressed upon entry into the gonad, were not expressed in cjPGCLCs.
source: Notably, DDX4 and DAZL, germ cell markers expressed upon entry into the gonad, were not expressed (Figure 6G), consistent with their lack of expression in pre-migratory cjPGCs at E50 (Figures 1E and 2E).
evidence: Supported by expression plot in Figure 6G showing no DDX4 and DAZL expression.

claim: The lack of DDX4 and DAZL expression in cjPGCLCs is consistent with their lack of expression in pre-migratory cjPGCs at E50.
source: Notably, DDX4 and DAZL, germ cell markers expressed upon entry into the gonad, were not expressed (Figure 6G), consistent with their lack of expression in pre-migratory cjPGCs at E50 (Figures 1E and 2E).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of gene expression patterns between cjPGCLCs and pre-migratory cjPGCs.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq was performed on three samples (OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, d2 and d6 cjPGCLCs) and 9098 cells were used for downstream analysis after QC validation and filtering.
source: To better define the lineage trajectory and transcriptomic dynamics accompanying cjPGCLC formation, we performed scRNA-seq on three samples (OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs, d2 and d6 cjPGCLCs [whole aggregates without FACS]). After QC validation and filtering, 9098 cells were used for downstream analysis (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by QC plots in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Transcriptomes of cells were aggregated and projected onto a tSNE after dimension reduction and clustering, which yielded six clusters.
source: Transcriptomes of cells were aggregated and projected onto a t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (tSNE) after dimension reduction and clustering, which yielded six clusters (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: Supported by tSNE plots in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B–D showing six clusters.

claim: Various off-target cells (cardiac, endoderm or endothelial lineages, macrophages) and a small fraction of apoptotic cells were observed in the scRNA-seq data.
source: As expected, we observed various off-target cells (cardiac, endoderm or endothelial lineages, macrophages) and a small fraction of apoptotic cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by heatmap and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F showing different cell types.

claim: A cell cluster that expressed pluripotency-associated genes (NANOG, POU5F1) and/or germ cell specifier genes (SOX17, TFAP2C) was identified, with its DEGs enriched with GO term such as 'germ cell development' or 'stem cell maintenance'.
source: Notably, we also identified a cell cluster that expressed pluripotency-associated (e.g., NANOG, POU5F1) and/or germ cell specifier genes (e.g., SOX17, TFAP2C), with its DEGs enriched with GO term such as 'germ cell development' or 'stem cell maintenance' (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: Supported by tSNE plots in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E showing expression of these genes, and heatmap in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F showing GO enrichment.

claim: The pluripotent/germ cell cluster primarily contains cjiPSCs and germline lineage and further subsetting revealed six subclusters.
source: This cluster primarily contains cjiPSCs and germline lineage and further subsetting revealed six subclusters (clusters 3, 1/4/6, and 2/5, consisting primarily of cjiPSCs, d2 or d6 cjPGCLCs, respectively) (Figure 7A and B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1G, H).
evidence: Supported by UMAP plots in Figure 7A and B showing subclusters, and dendrogram in Figure 7—figure supplement 1G.

claim: When projected on PHATE embedding, the subclusters aligned along the actual sample stages and pseudotime trajectory.
source: When projected on PHATE embedding, these subclusters aligned along the actual sample stages and pseudotime trajectory (Figure 7A–D), a finding further supported by RNA velocity analysis (Figure 7E).
evidence: Supported by PHATE embedding plots in Figure 7C and D showing alignment of subclusters along pseudotime, and RNA velocity plot in Figure 7E.

claim: Genes related to stem cell maintenance were downregulated along the pseudotime trajectory, suggestive of differentiation from cjiPSCs.
source: Accordingly, genes related to stem cell maintenance were downregulated along this trajectory, suggestive of differentiation from cjiPSCs (GO terms include 'stem cell population maintenance').
evidence: This is an inference based on the downregulation of stem cell maintenance genes along the trajectory.

claim: Early germ cell marker/specifier genes (KIT, NANOS3, DND1, SOX17, TFAP2C) or genes related to chromatin remodeling were upregulated along the pseudotime trajectory, suggestive of germ cell specification and accompanying epigenetic remodeling.
source: In contrast, early germ cell marker/specifier genes (e.g., KIT, NANOS3, DND1, SOX17, TFAP2C) or genes related to chromatin remodeling were upregulated, suggestive of germ cell specification and accompanying epigenetic remodeling (Figure 7F–H).
evidence: Supported by PHATE embedding plots in Figure 7F showing expression of these genes, and heatmap in Figure 7G showing GO enrichment.

claim: A number of mesodermal genes (EOMES, HAND1, MIXL1) were transiently upregulated in clusters 1/4/6, which were enriched with GO terms such as 'mesoderm formation'.
source: Consistent with bulk RNA-seq analyses, a number of mesodermal genes (e.g., EOMES, HAND1, MIXL1) were transiently upregulated in clusters 1/4/6, which were enriched with GO terms such as 'mesoderm formation' (Figure 7F and G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Supported by PHATE embedding plots in Figure 7F showing expression of mesodermal genes, and heatmap in Figure 7G showing GO enrichment.

claim: Many pluripotency-associated genes (NANOG, UTF1) were transiently downregulated during the transition from cjiPSCs to cjPGCLCs, similar to mouse but not human PGCLC specification.
source: In contrast, many pluripotency-associated genes (e.g., NANOG, UTF1) were transiently downregulated during this transition, similar to mouse but not human PGCLC specification (Figure 7F and H; Sasaki et al., 2015; Hayashi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by PHATE embedding plots in Figure 7F and expression dynamics plots in Figure 7H showing downregulation of NANOG and UTF1, and by citations to prior studies in mice and humans (Sasaki et al., 2015; Hayashi et al., 2011).

claim: E50 cjPGCs (cluster 7) juxtaposed with clusters 2/5 (d6 cjPGCLCs) in PHATE embedding.
source: As expected, E50 cjPGCs (cluster 7) juxtaposed with clusters 2/5 (d6 cjPGCLCs) in PHATE embedding (Figure 7I–K), and these clusters revealed a high correlation by Pearson correlation analysis (Figure 7L).
evidence: Supported by PHATE embedding plots in Figure 7I–K showing proximity of E50 cjPGCs and d6 cjPGCLCs, and Pearson correlation heatmap in Figure 7L.

claim: E50 cjPGCs and d6 cjPGCLCs revealed a high correlation by Pearson correlation analysis.
source: As expected, E50 cjPGCs (cluster 7) juxtaposed with clusters 2/5 (d6 cjPGCLCs) in PHATE embedding (Figure 7I–K), and these clusters revealed a high correlation by Pearson correlation analysis (Figure 7L).
evidence: Supported by Pearson correlation heatmap in Figure 7L showing high correlation between E50 cjPGCs and d6 cjPGCLCs.

claim: Many key germ cell markers/specifier genes are equally upregulated in both E50 cjPGCs and d6 cjPGCLCs.
source: Pairwise correlation analysis revealed that many key germ cell markers/specifier genes are equally upregulated in both cell types (Figure 7M).
evidence: Supported by scatter plot in Figure 7M showing similar expression levels of key germ cell genes in E50 cjPGCs and d6 cjPGCLCs.

claim: d6 cjPGCLCs were more proliferative/apoptotic whereas E50 cjPGCs upregulated genes were enriched in 'regulation of transcription from RNA polymerase II promoter'.
source: Notably, we found that d6 cjPGCLCs were more proliferative/apoptotic whereas E50 cjPGCs upregulated genes were enriched in 'regulation of transcription from RNA polymerase II promoter' (Figure 7M).
evidence: Supported by scatter plot and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 7M.

claim: A large fraction of PGCLC genes (genes upregulated in PGCLCs compared to iPSCs) were conserved between marmoset and humans, including genes associated with transcriptional regulation or protein ubiquitination.
source: We found that a large fraction of PGCLC genes were conserved, including genes associated with transcriptional regulation (most key germ cell specifier genes [e.g., TFAP2C, SOX17] were included in this category) or protein ubiquitination (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by scatter plots in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and B, and Venn diagram in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C showing overlap of PGCLC genes.

claim: Species-specific PGCLC genes were enriched in GO terms such as 'fatty acid homeostasis' (human PGCLC upregulated) or 'carbohydrate metabolic process' (marmoset PGCLC upregulated), which might indicate a species-specific metabolic requirement in early developing germ cells.
source: Notably, species-specific PGCLC genes were enriched in GO terms such as 'fatty acid homeostasis' (human PGCLC upregulated) or 'carbohydrate metabolic process' (marmoset PGCLC upregulated), which might indicate a species-specific metabolic requirement in early developing germ cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C.

claim: d4 PGCLCs showed a slight but significant reduction in 5mC levels (mean, ~63%) compared with OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs (mean, ~75%).
source: Similar to hPGCLCs (Sasaki et al., 2015; Murase et al., 2020), d4 PGCLCs showed a slight but significant reduction in 5mC levels (mean, ~63%) compared with OF/IWR1 cjiPSCs (mean, ~75%) (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 8A and scatter plot in Figure 8B showing DNA methylation levels, and by citations to prior studies in humans (Sasaki et al., 2015; Murase et al., 2020).

claim: cjPGCLCs in expansion culture exhibited further reduction in 5mC levels, bearing a 5mC level of ~50% at c30.
source: Notably, cjPGCLCs in expansion culture exhibited further reduction in 5mC levels, bearing a 5mC level of ~50% at c30 (Figure 8A and C).
evidence: Supported by boxplot in Figure 8A and scatter plot in Figure 8C showing DNA methylation levels.

claim: The dynamics of global 5mC levels during cjPGCLC induction and expansion is similar to that of humans.
source: Thus, the dynamics of global 5mC levels during cjPGCLC induction and expansion is similar to that of humans (Sasaki et al., 2015; Murase et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies in humans (Sasaki et al., 2015; Murase et al., 2020).

claim: DNMT3B was highly expressed in cjiPSCs, but exhibited a sharp downregulation upon cjPGCLC induction.
source: Among de novo DNA methyl transferases, DNMT3B was highly expressed in cjiPSCs, but exhibited a sharp downregulation upon cjPGCLC induction (Figure 8D).
evidence: Supported by expression dynamics plot in Figure 8D showing DNMT3B expression.

claim: DNMT3A showed modest downregulation upon cjPGCLC induction.
source: On the other hand, DNMT3A showed modest downregulation upon cjPGCLC induction, and DNMT3L was expressed only at low levels in all cells examined.
evidence: Supported by expression dynamics plot in Figure 8D showing DNMT3A expression.

claim: DNMT3L was expressed only at low levels in all cells examined.
source: On the other hand, DNMT3A showed modest downregulation upon cjPGCLC induction, and DNMT3L was expressed only at low levels in all cells examined.
evidence: Directly stated in the text.

claim: DNMT1 was expressed at a significant level in all cells analyzed.
source: Among the genes related to maintenance of DNA methylation, DNMT1 was expressed at a significant level in all cells analyzed, whereas UHRF1, which is responsible for the recruitment of DNMT1 into replication foci (Kagiwada et al., 2013; Sharif et al., 2007; Bostick et al., 2007), showed a marked reduction upon cjPGCLC induction (Figure 8D).
evidence: Supported by expression dynamics plot in Figure 8D showing DNMT1 expression.

claim: UHRF1 showed a marked reduction upon cjPGCLC induction.
source: Among the genes related to maintenance of DNA methylation, DNMT1 was expressed at a significant level in all cells analyzed, whereas UHRF1, which is responsible for the recruitment of DNMT1 into replication foci (Kagiwada et al., 2013; Sharif et al., 2007; Bostick et al., 2007), showed a marked reduction upon cjPGCLC induction (Figure 8D).
evidence: Supported by expression dynamics plot in Figure 8D showing UHRF1 expression, and by citations to prior studies on UHRF1 function (Kagiwada et al., 2013; Sharif et al., 2007; Bostick et al., 2007).
